name: Field Doctor-Style Chicken + Green Vegetable Risotto (Low FODMAP)
ingredients:
1505 g Chicken
825 g Whole grain rice
250 g Spinach
140 g Oyster Mushrooms
1/2 medium Courgettes
1/4 Green Peppers
23 g Broccoli
13 g Edamame (SOY bean)
6.9 g Fennel
3.8 g Peas
2/3 tsp White Wine [Water, White Wine, Salt, SULPHITES]
2/3 tsp Parmigiano (MILK) [MILK Salt, Microbial Enzymes]
1.7 g Chives
1/3 tsp Chicken Stock (Chicken Extract, Chicken Fat, Salt], Tapioca Starch, Yeast Extract, Herb Mix, Lemon Juice, Sea Salt, Black Pepper
directions:
1. Prep: Dice chicken; slice oyster mushrooms, courgette, green pepper, fennel and broccoli into small even pieces. Warm chicken stock with water and keep on a low simmer.

2. Chicken & veg: Soften chives in extra virgin olive oil, then brown the chicken. Add mushrooms, courgette, green pepper, fennel, broccoli, peas and edamame; cook until chicken is done and veg are tender-crisp. Tip out and keep warm.

3. Risotto rice: In the same pan, toast the wholegrain rice in a little more oil for 1–2 minutes. Deglaze with white wine and let it reduce. Add hot stock a ladle at a time, stirring, until the rice is creamy and just tender (slightly firm freezes better).

4. Finish: Fold the chicken and vegetables back in with spinach until wilted. Loosen with soy-free stock/water if needed; thicken lightly with tapioca slurry only if the risotto is too loose. Off heat, stir in hard cheese, lemon juice, herb mix, salt and pepper. Rest 2 minutes before portioning.
 
Cool, portion into 8, refrigerate up to 3 days or freeze; reheat until piping hot.

Ingredients: Chicken, Whole grain rice, Water, Spinach, Oyster Mushrooms, Courgette, Green Pepper, Broccoli...

Home recreation inspired by Field Doctor Chicken + Green Vegetable Risotto (Low FODMAP) (~418 g ready meal). Scaled to 8 portions. Not an official Field Doctor recipe. https://www.fielddoctor.co.uk/products/chicken-pea-asparagus-risotto-low-fodmap
notes:
REVERSE-ENGINEERED from Field Doctor published ingredients for personal home cooking only. Official meal is Monash Low FODMAP certified at single-serve size.

Scaling notes
Scaled for 8 portions from Field Doctor single serve (~418 g x 8 = 3344 g).
Unlabelled amounts inferred from UK descending-weight ingredient order (each item <= the one above and >= the one below; leftover mass shared on that basis, not equally).
Spoon measures use ingredient density (g per tsp) then round to kitchen fractions.
Amounts above 50 g are rounded to the nearest 5 g for cooking convenience.
Sweet peppers ~140 g each; carrots ~80 g; sweet potatoes ~130 g; courgettes ~175 g; aubergines ~250 g; swedes ~800 g; plum tomatoes = 400 g tins; lemon ~45 ml / lime ~30 ml juice.
Duplicate label ingredients merged (higher amount kept).
Liquid for home cooking: cook rice, quinoa, pasta, noodles and potatoes in water as you normally would (salt the water; drain where appropriate). For sauces, braises and stir-fry glazes, add water or stock gradually until the consistency is right — do not try to measure the ready-meal's residual water.
Low FODMAP: no onion or garlic bulbs — use chives / green tops only. Inspired recreation from Field Doctor ingredients, not an official recipe.
Chives listed in grams to match fresh packs (e.g. Waitrose Cooks' Ingredients Chives, 20 g).
Ready-meal residual water was ~455 g (inferred ~13.60% from list order) and is not listed as an ingredient.
Oil for home cooking: where Extra Virgin Olive Oil was only a cooking fat on the label, it is omitted from ingredients — fry, soften, sear or roast in extra virgin olive oil as needed. It is kept as an ingredient on richer/oil-forward dishes (e.g. pesto-style sauces or high oil content).
Ready-meal residual Extra Virgin Olive Oil was ~2.1 g (inferred ~0.06% from list order) and is treated as cooking fat (fry in extra virgin olive oil) rather than a measured ingredient.
